description: Building an onboard "health companion" for astronauts: biomedical monitoring (heart rate, HRV, sleep, bone density, radiation) shown as a gamified "Mission Health Score" instead of a clinical dashboard, plus a light VR/3D layer for biofeedback — helping astronauts act on their health without real-time ground contact. I'm a biomedical engineer leading the science. Looking for devs, designers, and gamers. Beginners welcome
summary:
AURA is a personal health and readiness dashboard designed to help astronauts understand their health, build awareness, support healthier routines, and learn how to respond to emergencies. It combines live wearable heart-rate and heart-rate-variability measurements with recorded sleep, oxygen saturation, and activity information across two horizons: Daily Readiness and Long-Term Mission Health. 

The interactive prototype integrates NASA Curiosity RAD radiation observations, NASA-grounded bone-health modeling, and NASA flight-crew physiological data to test the processing pipeline. AURA translates these inputs into visual insights, health-support alerts, and explanations through a conversational companion with natural voice narration. Users can record recommended actions and reassess their measurements afterward.
AURA also includes voice-guided emergency protocol training using a fictional medical scenario. Through action-based rewards, I encourage appropriate routines and teamwork, recognizing participation rather than better biomarker values. Optional weekly VR training forms part of my roadmap.
AURA addresses the challenge by making complex health information accessible and actionable. I believe AURA can support astronauts’ wellbeing and preparedness by connecting daily awareness, long-term monitoring, and emergency practice, while clearly distinguishing measured data, modeled estimates, and simulations. It supports health understanding without replacing medical expertise.
details:
AURA is a personal health and readiness companion for astronauts. My goal is to help them understand their measurements, build health awareness, maintain appropriate routines, and practice how to respond to emergencies.

What it does and how it works

AURA organizes information into two complementary health horizons:

  • Daily Readiness: wearable heart rate and, when available, heart-rate variability, together with recorded sleep, oxygen saturation, and activity.
  • Long-Term Mission Health: historical NASA radiation observations and a NASA-grounded bone-health reference model.

I connected Kyto and Huawei wearable sensors through Bluetooth. Kyto provides heart rate and beat intervals for HRV processing; the Huawei integration currently provides heart rate. Sleep, oxygen saturation, and activity can be entered as dated context.

AURA checks measurement quality and builds a personal baseline from valid resting assessments. It highlights relevant deviations and presents supportive next actions, such as reviewing rest, considering mindfulness, or checking adherence to an approved exercise plan. Users can record an action and collect a new assessment to compare measurements. A change is reported as an observation—not proof that the action improved health.

The conversational companion explains the selected health information and answers typed questions. Natural voice narration makes its responses and recommendations easier to access.

How I used NASA resources

I integrated three distinct sources of evidence:

  • Curiosity RAD observations: to calculate cumulative environmental radiation exposure over the covered intervals of a historical Mars dataset.
  • NASA bone-health research: to inform a modeled reference trajectory and explain the importance of countermeasures.
  • NASA flight-crew physiological recordings: to test ECG ingestion, beat detection, and signal-quality processing.

A sources panel explaining provenance, processing, and limitations is included. These resources are not presented as measurements of an individual astronaut’s radiation dose or bone density.

Benefits and intended impact

AURA is designed to bring measurements, explanations, actions, and follow-up into one interface. Its intended impact is to strengthen health awareness and support consistent routines while making complex information easier to interpret.

AURA also provides voice-guided emergency protocol training through a fictional dizziness scenario. Users follow a checklist, confirm actions, record observations, and prepare a simulated handover. This demonstrates a training workflow; it is not a validated operational emergency procedure.

The rewards area encourages appropriate actions and teamwork. My central rule is: no points for better biomarkers. Recognition comes from following appropriate routines, reviewing information, and completing readiness practice. The current crew board is locally maintained and uses optional, consented participation.

Tools, languages, hardware, and software

  • HTML and CSS for the dashboard and responsive visual design.
  • JavaScript modules and Web Bluetooth for sensor connectivity, signal processing, visualization, alerts, reassessment, and rewards.
  • PHP and WordPress for server-side AI access, private configuration, and expiring access codes.
  • OpenAI APIs for conversational explanations and natural speech.
  • Python for dataset preparation and verification.
  • Kyto and Huawei wearables for live physiological input.
  • FileZilla and Porkbun hosting to deploy the dashboard.
  • Codex to assist with development, iteration, and testing.

What makes it creative and what I considered

AURA brings daily health awareness and long-term mission health monitoring into one experience. Its distinctive feature is the connection between understanding information and taking action: an explainable conversational companion, voice-guided recommendations, reassessment, and rewards for appropriate routines and teamwork. AURA also incorporates emergency practice through a fictional medical scenario, connecting health monitoring with readiness training. Its roadmap extends this approach to optional weekly VR challenges, competency assessment, and adaptive retraining tailored to skills that need improvement.

Throughout development, I considered privacy, missing data, sensor limitations, accessibility, connectivity, and the risk of overstating what measurements can establish. I kept real measurements, historical NASA data, modeled estimates, and fictional scenarios clearly separated.

Explore AURA

  1. Open AURA Dashboard and click Explore demo.
  2. In Companion, click Meet AURA. Type a question, accept the data-sharing checkbox, and select Send to AURA AI. Use Read aloud to hear the answer.
  3. Open the Health support icon → Preview all 4 scenarios. Play each recommendation and use Next notification.
  4. Open Medical Assist · training and follow the fictional emergency checklist. Confirm each step to continue.
  5. Visit Readiness rewards → Preview rewards to explore personal and crew recognition.
  6. Explore NASA sources, Evidence & Testing, and the VR training roadmap.

Internet access is required for AI answers and voice playback.
